posts.title: Following a slow request across services with Aspire and an AI agent
posts.description: In the previous post, the slow code and the slow queries were in the same service. This time, a request goes through a web shop, a Redis cache, and a catalog service. The trace shows where the time goes, the logs say what the code decided, and the agent needs both. posts.title: Finding slow requests with Aspire and an AI agent
posts.description: The previous posts in this series answered questions about one process at one moment: why it crashed, what it waits for, what holds its memory. "Which requests are slow?" is a different kind of question. The answer is spread over time and often over several processes, and no dump contains it. Distributed traces do. posts.title: Debugging a running .NET application with WinDbg and an AI agent
posts.description: Every post in this series so far started from a file: a dump, a gcdump, a trace. That works as long as the answer is in memory at the moment the file is written. Some answers never are. A dump can show that a value is wrong. It cannot show who wrote it, because by the time the dump is taken, the write is long gone.
